wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.

admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by capability actions. The authorizing actions are exactly the ones whose target_event_kinds list this kind in capability-action-registry; there is no second per-event list. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.conditional: Admission is selected from the event row's closed admission_variants. Receivers evaluate every non-otherwise predicate using admission_predicate_contract: exactly one match selects that variant, more than one match is fail-closed, and zero matches selects the single final otherwise variant. The otherwise branch is a fallback and is not counted as a simultaneously matching predicate. Each selected variant applies its own admission class and capabilities.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.delegated_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for a PCR ak.realm.create with no did_inception ref and with both executed_by and authorization_ref. For purpose=agent_control the immutable accepted controller-authored ak.agent.provision is resolved by its whole-value claim of retype(this EventId, realm); the genesis MUST NOT carry a backward agent_provision ref, which would create an EventId cycle. The verifier cross-binds the complete actor/controller AccountIds, PCR delegation and provision payload before materializing Agent status. An explicitly organization-governed purpose=principal_control branch proves its separate accepted organization authority. A self-principal or generic realm.create capability substitution is rejected. This class never authorizes a following device-authorize slot by itself.
admission_class_definitions.applet_managed_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for purpose=applet_managed_control ak.realm.create carrying exactly one critical refs[] role=applet_managed_actor_provision. The referenced accepted ak.applet.managed_actor.provision is immutable and cross-binds the exact account ActorId, applet/service/registration/authority, role, event-derived realm_id and object.initial_resolution. executed_by MUST equal the provision service_id and authorization_ref MUST equal its applet_authority_ref. It never substitutes Agent or human PCR admission.
admission_class_definitions.deny: Explicit fail-closed admission branch. Selection always rejects the Event as failed_precondition/schema_violation and MUST NOT consult capabilities or alternate proof paths.
admission_class_definitions.registration_anchor: Admitted only for self-principal PCR genesis using durable registration-time DID control evidence and one critical did_inception ref. The verifier validates the accepted-at adapter/method evidence and project(did)=actor_id; current DID state after registration is irrelevant.
admission_class_definitions.pcr_recovery: Admitted only for ak.device.reanchor under the account-local lineage's accepted PCR recovery policy/session and monotonic generation CAS. did_root is merely one optional policy-enabled factor. A current DID proof without the matching account-local lineage and policy cannot enter this class.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_agent_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_agent_provision pointing to an accepted ak.agent.provision Event. Used solely for the controller-to-own-Agent Direct Conversation branch, which has no Contact round. The verifier cross-binds participants to exactly that controller and Agent, requires the Direct Conversation profile rather than a PCR profile, checks the controller binding is current, and fixes founder = controller so the Agent runtime key never needs Direct Conversation founding scope. This role is structurally exclusive with direct_conversation_contact_round and with the Agent PCR agent_provision role.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_contact_round pointing to the portable Contact round evidence bundle and its continuity chain to the pair's root Contact round. The verifier derives founder from the root Contact round (normal branch: the root-round responder; glare branch: the full signed request Event author ActorId referenced by requests[0], never the Station receipt issuer_id; requests MUST be strictly ascending by the complete request_event_ref wire string UTF-8 unsigned bytes, with duplicate Event refs rejected regardless of receipt digest and no receiver-side sorting or deduplication), then requires created_by == actor_id == founder, recomputes pair_key from sorted_pair_member_ids and the trust domain, and pins the Direct Conversation profile, exact-two participants and the create-locked encryption and history baseline. Accepted-at Contact round validity and current directional Contact gates are evaluated separately so Event validity never depends on delivery order.
admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a proof bound to the subject principal's identity: either the subject's DID-bound signature / proof of possession, or a currently valid delegated-control proof whose authorization_ref is bound by the subject DID Document. Reducer MUST verify actor == subject, executed_by/authorization_ref when delegated, a fresh replay-protected proof, and that the accepted-at delegation purpose/scope explicitly covers the target event kind, resource and operation; mere presence of a DID-bound delegation is never sufficient. No Realm capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing, stale, unbound, purpose-inapplicable or scope-inapplicable proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.sidecar_account_self_authored_proof: Admitted only when Event actor_id is the account branch and its complete AccountId is the authenticated controller account. The reducer derives controller_account_id byte-for-byte from actor_id.account_id, uses (realm_id, controller_account_id) as the singleton key, and rejects the service actor branch with sidecar_create_denied before revealing existence. The same exact AccountId binds Sidecar membership, MLS genesis and participant authority; principal-only equality is forbidden.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-ID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.

admission_predicate_contract.selector_semantics: All selector fields in one non-otherwise when object are ANDed. payload_path is relative to Event.payload; const uses exact JSON value equality, while not_const matches inequality or an absent path. top_level_fields_present requires every listed Event Envelope field. ref_* selectors evaluate Event.refs after schema validation. Unknown selectors, missing companion selectors, multiple matching non-otherwise variants, or evaluation errors are fail-closed.

registry_rules: Every standard ak.* Event.kind admitted through Event Envelope MUST appear in this registry and resolve to exactly one closed payload schema.
An accepted durable Event becomes shared history only when the current authority includes its exact bytes in a signed RealmCommit for the Event's own Realm, Circle, or Sidecar stream.
Stream identity is derived from the Event's closed scope. Realm, each Circle, and each Sidecar have independent commit streams; no Realm-global total chain exists.
Event carries no chain predecessor or authority-commit proof. Only RealmCommit carries previous_commit_ref, and only within the same stream.
Reducers derive typed current results by replaying committed Events in stream position order. Account-private material is outside shared authority-commit streams.

result_writes[] is the machine contract for which typed current results one Event kind writes, in what order, and under which closed condition; zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.1 and zh/authz/capabilities.md section 10 read it as the source of truth, and tools/artifact_lint:result_write_contracts validates every declared row. COVERAGE IS PARTIAL AND THIS IS A KNOWN GAP: 12 of the 139 reducer_input kinds declare it (ak.agent.key.authorize, ak.call.recording.start, ak.call.state, ak.call.summary, ak.capability.grant, ak.member.state, ak.mls.commit, ak.mls.genesis, ak.realm.create, ak.realm.history_access, ak.realm.profile, ak.strand.create); the remaining 127 still have no machine-readable reducer contract, so their registered writes exist only in prose. Normative prose MUST NOT cite result_writes[] for a kind that does not declare it -- a citation without a row is the exact defect this array was added to close. Extend coverage kind by kind and shrink this note; do not narrow the rule to make it read as complete.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ak.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.
payload_schema_contract.explicit_binding_rule: Each active standard event kind declares exactly one payload_schema_ref, and the Event Envelope dispatch selects that exact location. Missing, dangling, duplicate, or divergent bindings fail closed. Consumers MUST NOT infer a payload schema from kind spelling or naming conventions.

Controller-signed one-shot publication authorization in the target Realm safety sequence. approved_event_id binds the complete pre-authored Event. The same confirmed command allocates (controller ActorId, approval_nonce) once; it is not a reusable private approval followed by receiver-local consumption. The original Event remains ordinary data and requires this exact confirmation only when its explicit approval constraint applies.

Agent-initiated draft proposal. Submitted by agent runtime; Station materializes accepted drafts into controller-owned ak.agent.draft.v1 account-data after capability / policy / accountability / risk check. MUST NOT enter shared Realm history.

Agent key authorization is a commit-ordered projection security command with complete explicit revocation set representation. Same-key replacement removes all authorization dots visible at the signed basis and adds one replacement dot, after exact revision and authority checks at execution. Competing replacements cannot survive as concurrent permission heads. Runtime replacement pairs a new raw key and revokes prior active keys in the same confirmed transaction.

result_writes.notes: identity/key-management.md section 3.6.1 fixes the order: the reducer MUST first project, for every payload.supersedes[] item, a remove of the observed canonical Event dot named by that item's authorized_event_ref on the OLD key subject, and only then add the new authorization. So this is write_index 0 and the add below is write_index 1. The subject moves per item, which is why the selector reads item.key_id while the add reads payload.key_id; payload.supersedes is the exact complete active authorization set at expected_revision, bounded at 256 items, so the loop is closed rather than open. Removing the exact observed dot rather than the whole observed set is what makes same-key re-authorization and replacement supersede provable from the signed RealmCommit without a service-private key table.

identity/key-management.md section 3.6.1: the stable element tag is the canonical <event_id>:<write_index> dot of models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2 and never a bare event_id, and the element value is the complete authorize payload. The subject MUST be the SDK composite_subject([agent_id, key_id]) and MUST NOT be spelled by string concatenation or as a diagnostic subject; agent_key_result.selector carries the two components separately for the same reason. ak.agent.key.revoke is the family's second normative writer and is deliberately still unregistered: section 3.6.1 tells it to remove every active authorize dot observed at expected_revision and then add a revocation boundary marker, but agent_key_authorization_entry is a closed {tag_id, value} with no authorize/revoke discriminator, so 'every active authorize dot' and 'every observed dot' are only the same set until a re-authorization follows an earlier revoke. Registering a bare keyed_set_remove_observed, whose match-less form removes every observed element in scope (zh/models/pins.md section 3), would silently drop that earlier boundary marker, so the shape waits on a prose ruling rather than on a guess.

event_kinds.payload: Invite create. Directed v1 genesis payloads carry the exact invitee_account_id, introduction_evidence_digest and expires_at; the Invite ID is derived from this Event. Delivery resolves invitee_account_id.station_id outside durable Realm state. Raw locator tokens, route material and invite_receive_policy state MUST NOT enter the durable Realm event. The Event atomically claims the Realm live-target slot invite_live_target keyed by canonical_json(payload.invitee_account_id) and MUST carry that typed current result's expected_revision null precondition; a second live directed invite for the same account is rejected with failed_precondition and reason_code invite_live_target_occupied, writes nothing and does not enter canonical history.

Carries the terminal or send_failed transition of a directed or third-party invite. payload.invitee_account_id is present exactly when the target Invite stores one and target_state is not send_failed; send_failed keeps the invite live, so the schema forbids the field there and no slot write is derived. When present the Event atomically releases the invite_live_target slot keyed by canonical_json(payload.invitee_account_id) and MUST carry its expected_revision precondition equal to the stored create_event_id.

Realm-scoped MemberIdentity segment replacement event. Append-only log entry that may supersede prior ak.member.identity.update events via payload.replaces[] without overloading ak.profile.update patch semantics. The event always enters the append-only log: proof and replacement validation are consumption/verification-surface semantics, not reducer rejection. When the MemberIdentity proof fails validation (payload_digest mismatch, signature failure, or verification_method not controlled by subject_id), receivers surface reason=member_identity_proof_invalid and MUST NOT promote the event to a verified display identity. When a replaces[] entry payload_digest or (realm_id, member_id, segment) does not match, only that replacement edge is invalid (surface member_identity_replacement_digest_mismatch); receivers MUST NOT remove the referenced event from the effective set on that basis. Only the optional expected_state_digest guard retains reducer semantics: when expected_state_digest does not equal the current effective-set digest, the server/reducer MUST reject or quarantine the event with reason=member_identity_state_mismatch. See zh/sync/client-sync.md §8.1.

Realm membership state. Agent join/cleanup Events carry an exact agent_controller_binding. Effective Agent membership additionally AND-gates the controller authority pair and bound join Event generation, lifecycle and provision/accountability validity. Controller terminal transitions never synthesize this Event: self leave uses the registered atomic agent_membership_cascade unit; third-party emergency removal freezes a durable exact-set cleanup intent and the original initiator later signs the complete Agent leave set.

result_writes.notes: models/realm-and-space.md section 2.7 says ak.member.state writes member_state under the complete payload.member_id ActorId, and the account branch compares both AccountId components, so the subject is the canonical JSON of the whole ActorId and never a bare DID. The shared materialized membership FSM of models/common-fields.md section 4.5 is a four-state register over join/knock/leave/ban, so the projection is a whole-value set of the one member the payload carries. member_state_result.value also admits an optional joined_at, but no normative paragraph names a writer for it; leaving it unprojected keeps the registry honest instead of inventing envelope.created_at as its source. ak.invite.accept drives the same leave -> join edge in that FSM table and is not registered here: its payload identifies the accepting party by AccountId and the retype to the complete ActorId this subject requires has no expressible source in the current selector grammar.

Single registered carrier that settles one Relation primary conflict domain. The ordinary causal repair Event retains exactly one still-valid candidate head of the covered group or voids the covered set after proving it observed the complete conflict domain; and ak.relation.update / ak.relation.tombstone each address one Relation and therefore cannot prove the author covered the complete head set. payload.conflict_domain is the whole typed current result subject, payload.baseline is the frozen data-plane completeness commitment the receiver rebuilds independently, and payload.outcome is closed to retain_candidate or void_all. The Event writes only the registered group ordinary causal typed current result; Relation content stays on its own data typed results and the active-edge projection reads both.
admission_checks: conflict_domain resolves to a directly writable relation-kind-registry.json shape whose registered primary_conflict_domain equals conflict_domain.domain_kind; a derived_projection shape is rejected with schema_violation (reason=relation_kind_contains_derived or relation_kind_watches_derived)

the receiver rebuilds the complete active candidate head set of the domain from its own accepted Relation history under this Event's frozen predecessor view, recomputes the chained commitment of zh/models/relation.md section 6.3, and requires byte equality with payload.baseline.members_digest and payload.baseline.member_count; a missing member, a superseded head, a duplicate, a foreign-domain member or any later group change rejects the Event with failed_precondition reason=relation_conflict_baseline_stale and zero typed current result writes

when payload.baseline.member_event_ids is present it MUST equal that rebuilt set element by element in canonical bytewise-ascending order; member_count above 64 omits the inline list and is proven by members_digest alone, and the ordinary 16-head diagnostic bound MUST NOT be applied to this evidence

a retain_candidate outcome names a retained_event_id that belongs to this Event's own baseline; a name outside the covered set is rejected with failed_precondition reason=relation_conflict_baseline_stale

the actor independently holds the registered ak.relation.resolve capability over every candidate in the covered group and its scope; holding ak.relation.update on one member never authorizes adjudicating the others
Relation conflict resolution is an ordinary causal successor. It observes the complete intended domain candidate set and does not reset security state or invoke an unregistered recovery authority.
